g.text: Model transformation across supersaturation: viscoelastic phase separation (VPS) continuum
Structural and mathematical evolution grounded in multi-scale composite SAXS datasets (q in [0.002, 2.5] nm⁻¹)
Initial reactant concentration [Ca²⁺]₀ (mM) → increasing thermodynamic supersaturation ln(S_ACC)
Isolated ACC spheres and sheared droplets
ACC spheres: 100% | Fractal gel: 0% | Tanaka PNC: 0%
Mode 1 (28% @ 21 nm) + Mode 2 (72% @ 60 nm); 0% gel network & PNC mesh
Primary network nodes and ACC spheres
Coexistence of network and discrete spheres
Dynamic evolution: 96% ACC (0.06 s) → 76% fractal gel (10.9 s)
Fractal gel: 76% | Tanaka PNC mesh: 24% (0% spheres)
Transient viscoelastic PNC mesh (R_pnc ≈ 1.46 nm); discrete spheres 0%
Percolating spinodal network, coarsening droplets, and PNC mesh
Time-resolved percolation (351 frames, 15 ms/frame; compares to ND-i-001 at pH 11.3)
I_tot(q) = P_prim · S_net + I_drop + I_fluc(q) + bkg
• Time-resolved percolation: finite ξ = 46.7 nm at frame 0 → continuous gel (ξ → ∞)
• Tanaka volume shrinking: D_m(t) compacts from 1.881 to 1.925 (|dD_m| ≤ 0.004)
• PNC viscoelastic mesh: ξ_fluc: 2.72 to 2.84 nm; A_fluc: 0.142 to 0.197 cm⁻¹
• pH 11.3 pure counterpart (ND-i-001): instant quench (D_m = 2.33, ξ = 735 nm, t_ind < 0.06 s)
Pure CaCO₃ benchmark resolving continuous pre-percolation and PNC mesh dynamics
VPS: Stress relaxation and phase inversion
Fractal gel: 73% | Tanaka PNC mesh: 26% | Droplets: 1% (0% spheres)
Tanaka viscoelastic fluctuation mesh (ξ_fluc ≈ 2.7 nm) vitrifies into percolated gel nodes
• Adsorption lowers interfacial tension γ: enlarges nodes R_prim: 3.5 to 6.59 nm
• Extended network cutoff: expands ξ: 735 to 1,190 nm; open fractal D_m: 2.33 to 2.10
• Only sample containing transition metal dopant; all other series are pure CaCO₃
Stationary phase inversion droplets (universal across series)
⟨R_large⟩ ≈ 2.2 to 3.5 μm, φ_large ≈ (3.0 to 6.0) × 10⁻⁵ formed by mechanical strut rupture and capillary break-up
Viscoelastic mesh in the context of prenucleation clusters (PNCs)
High-q fluctuation length ξ_fluc ≈ 1.5 to 3.0 nm reflects the transient mesh of entangled, hydrated PNC oligomers prior to solid ACC condensation
Data processing responsible: Tomasz Stawski, tomasz.stawski@bam.de | Viscoelastic phase separation (VPS) framework | Data: ESRF ID02
